why: Found by route 2: Wikidata Q25552821 is labelled «Никифор Антиохийский», which is this folder's own stored Russian form exactly, and its P373 is Category:Saint Nikephoros of Antioch, whose one file this is and which is also the entity's P18. 453x600, just over the floor. The martyr of Antioch kept 9 February in all four of this corpus's calendars; the title's «Св. Никифор» names him and no other Nicephorus answers to the Antioch by-name.

Found by route 2: Wikidata Q12755135, described 'Egyptian hegumen', answered the search for 'Memnon the Wonderworker' and carries P373 Category:Saint Memnon with this as its single file and its P18. 1167x1200. The folder stores «Мемнон Египетский» and types venerable/abbot/wonderworker, and the file's own title is «Мемнон Чудотворец», the wonderworker — the Egyptian abbot kept 29 April in the Russian, Romanian and Serbian calendars and 28 April in the Greek.

why: Found by route 4, a hand alias route 2 surfaced sideways: searching 'Erastus' on Wikidata returns the given name and four American politicians, but Category:Erastus (given name) lists Category:Erastus of Corinth among its subcategories, and that is the apostle's own category. The file is a Menaion Reader plate and BOTH halves of the plate identity rule hold: the code 03103 is month 3 counted from September, which is November, and day 10 — the 10 November this folder keeps in all four calendars — and the title names «Ераст», the folder's own stored Russian form. 854x1711. It is a TWO-figure plate, Erastus with Quartus, who is kept the same day; Erastus is the first named. The category's other files are the Corinth Erastus inscription, a whole November menaion tablet, and a Menologion of Basil II miniature of six apostles together.
